keyFindings.description: Lagging was not the only cause of its kind, and the exclusion list caught one of two. ghautomerge.Disappeared - 'pull request #N of <repo> is no longer armed or queued at READY's head <sha>, and its timeline names no removal since: the daemon waits for GitHub to record one' (ghautomerge.go:413) - declares Is(wait.ErrWaiting) at :418 and is returned by removal() at removal.go:147, which Submit returns from its armed branch, so it reaches rememberWait through readyMerge's general error arm and satisfies every term of the new gate. The notice it would carry says 'The merge has not been withdrawn, the issue stays in awaiting_merge and the daemon goes on submitting it', on the premise the function's own doc states, that nothing has gone wrong with the row. With Disappeared the arm the daemon placed is gone from GitHub and the row is reading the timeline rather than submitting, so both clauses are false; and when the removal is real and only the timeline lagged, the next run reads Removed, which permanentRefusal ends with merge-stalled's sibling merge-removed saying the daemon submits it no further - two tellings about one row within a minute, the second contradicting the first, which is exactly what round ten closed for Lagging. When the read was merely ahead of itself, the one notice has been spent on a transient and the genuine wait that follows is never told. The remedy is not a third exclusion: make the gate an allowlist of the causes whose premise the notice states - Armed, Unmergeable, Merging - so a wait type added later is silent by default rather than wrong by default. That also deletes the gate's now-dead last term: with the stalled Lagging half already excluded, permanentRefusal can only be true for Refused or Removed, neither of which declares Is(wait.ErrWaiting) nor wraps a waiting error, so the earlier conjunct has already short-circuited and !permanentRefusal can no longer change the value of warn.

Still reads 'since the merger's READY check posts a conflicting head whose required checks all succeeded'. After this change READY reads no check of the head at all, so the clause states a reader that no longer exists. It is the same class the diff corrects twice in this very file (:129-134 and :474-478) and once in the requiredchecks package doc, and the branch's own sweep cannot catch it: the retired-phrase list is READY_CHECKS_NOT_GREEN, 'no check is required on' and 'refused at READY'. required_checks.go:69's 'the reader READY uses' is the same family and is already on the fast-follow line; this one is in a file the diff edits for exactly this reason, so it belongs with the fix rather than after it.

roundTenFindingsVerified: Finding 1 (the warn gate admitting an unstalled Lagging) fixed in 2f833383049eb6e65ab8b4be36992031a12c6dc3 as prescribed, with TestAREADYMergeDisagreementSpendsNoWaitingNotice driving a CLOSED read past mergeWaitWarn and asserting no notice and warned false, then an OPEN/BLOCKED read asserting exactly one notice naming BLOCKED and not CLOSED. I read the test for whether it would fail without the gate change: in phase one pullJSON stamps updatedAt at now against a clock at now, so Stalled is false and permanentRefusal does not fire, and every remaining term is true - the assertion of zero notices is what the old gate would break. The doc comment now carries the reason rather than only the stalled half.

Finding 2 (the Verification paragraph stating the head's CI as a present fact) fixed in the same commit: the paragraph now states an observation with a time and a named head, says in terms that it states no verdict for this head, names what the earlier wording claimed and why it was wrong, and the withdrawn 'by run id and never by head' instruction is gone from it.
myOwnLinesCorrected: The Look at first line I wrote in round ten described the Verification paragraph as stating this head's CI as a present fact. 2f833383 rewrote that paragraph to say the opposite, so my pointer now asserts of the body the property this branch exists to delete while the paragraph it points at denies it; and its auto_merge.go:164 citation drifted six lines when that commit added comment lines, so it no longer lands on the gate. Both corrected in this round's body edit.
whatIVerifiedMyself: The Disappeared path of finding 1 traced through removal.go:147, ghautomerge.go:403-418 and Submit's armed branch rather than taken from the report.
The dead last term of the gate reasoned out from Refused and Removed declaring no Is and being returned bare.
review.go:67-68 read in context against the two corrections the same diff makes in the same file.

The body's Size line: it says +1665 and claims to have been re-read at this head; GitHub answers 1675 additions at c1d161f9. Minor, disclosed by its own sentence that the figure moves with every push, and not carried as a finding - but it is the third round in which a body figure outlived the push that made it true.

I read the required checks of the code commit on GitHub myself before deciding and carry no verdict or run id forward as what the head holds now: the required set is lint, typecheck, test and pr-title with no branch-protection checks, every required name's newest run at the code commit had completed and succeeded when I read it, nothing there was failed, cancelled or timed out, the only lane still running was the non-required dispatch check, and the compare from that commit to the pull request's head returned handoffsOnly true over two files.
residualRiskNoted: With Lagging excluded, a disagreement whose pull request keeps being touched never satisfies Stalled, since that reads GitHub's latest updatedAt on every run, so such a row now raises neither merge-stalled nor merge-waiting and retries indefinitely. That is the fix's intent and the alarm is not gone - Lagging is not Routine, so the outbox keeps logging it at warning level - but the operator log is now its only signal, and the allowlist in finding 1 does not change that either way. Recorded on the pull request's risk list rather than carried as a finding.

Its first finding is the dead permanentRefusal term and the five-term conjunction, which folds into finding 1's allowlist; its third is that the new test hand-rolls a GitHub stand-in the suite already has in newMergeGitHub, losing that helper's bearer recording and head assertion, which is on the fast-follow line.
thermonuclear.perHalf: Both halves returned a body with a verdict line on their first invocation. Neither needed a re-run.

fastFollow: The new test builds its own httptest server with a mutex and a mutable flag where newMergeGitHub already answers differently per read, losing that helper's bearer recording and its assertion that a merge mutation names READY's head.
required_checks.go:69 still calls requiredchecks.Required the reader READY uses.
The literal pin forces a 187-character line in three otherwise narrow documents; the CI-line guard's negation lookbehind does not compose with its own re- prefix; neither guard reads docs/solutions.
classify.Judge lost its last caller outside its package; readyChecks reads no check; rememberWait keeps a positional bool its callee can derive; the compare command is hand-maintained in two files.
